new_candidates.body:
Drake can silently assign the wrong pose to an SDF <frame> when its attached_to target is a joint or a frame declared later in the model.

The parser initially calculates the frame’s pose relative to its named attachment target. If that target has no frame in the plant yet, the parser instead attaches the frame to the target’s resolved body or implicit model frame—but previously kept the original offset. This drops the target’s translation and rotation.
For example, suppose F1 is at [0, 0, 3] with a 90° yaw, and F2 is one meter along F1’s x-axis. If F2 is declared first, the old parser places it at [1, 0, 0] with no rotation. The correct pose is [0, 1, 3] with a 90° yaw.

This was discovered incidentally by Codex while working on another feature. I'll follow up with a PR to fix this.
new_candidates.title: [parser] SDFormat parser drops attachment-frame poses for joints and forward references
